3. Data Sources

Observed Data

Historical data come from a Rutgers University Global Snow Lab (GSL) reanalysis of digitized maps produced by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) using their Interactive Multisensor Snow and Ice Mapping System (IMS).

Model Outputs

This pairing presents outputs from 13 global climate models (GCMs) within the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP) Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) suite. While other pairings with GCM outputs use a standardized set of 16 GCMs, three of those GCMs have not published results for snow cover, so this feature is based on the other 13 GCMs from the set. Specific runs are noted in parentheses:

  • BCC-CSM2-MR (r1i1p1f1)
  • CanESM5 (r1i1p1f1)
  • EC-Earth3 (r1i1p1f1)
  • FGOALS-g3 (r1i1p1f1)
  • INM-CM4.8 (r1i1p1f1)
  • INM-CM5.0 (r1i1p1f1)
  • IPSL-CM6A-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MIROC6 (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-HR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MPI-ESM1-2-LR (r1i1p1f1)
  • MRI-ESM2-0 (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-LM (r1i1p1f1)
  • NorESM2-MM (r1i1p1f1)

Specifically, this analysis uses the “snc” variable, which represents the proportion of each grid cell covered by snow.

4. Data Availability

Observed Data

Complete weekly and monthly snow cover extent data for North America (excluding Greenland) are publicly available for users to download from the GSL website. A complete description of these data can also be found on the GSL website. The underlying NOAA gridded maps are also publicly available. To obtain these maps, visit the National Snow and Ice Data Center website. EPA’s Snow Cover indicator uses the published source linked above. However, as a result of a lack of alignment with the modeled results, the project team worked with GSL to procure a different historical data set for this pairing: a recently developed analysis using a higher-resolution grid than GSL’s core products. This higher-resolution product was provided to the project team by GSL personnel (Robinson and Estilow, 2021).

Model Outputs

CMIP6 monthly climate model outputs were retrieved from the publicly available CMIP6 data archive hosted by the Earth System Grid Federation. The overall technical documentation [to be linked] for this effort identifies the organizational ownership and direct source links for each of the individual models.
